newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices up on retail sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices up on retail sales.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose 1/4 to 3/8 of a point in early trade Thursday as U.S. Treasuries shot higher after an unexpected drop in May retail sales.
"That was a great number for the market," one trader said, adding that a firm dollar and bigger than expected rise in weekly jobless claims also helped.
"Everything is sounding good for bonds right now," he said. "Everything is green on the screen."

The government said U.S. retail sales slipped 0.1 percent in May. Economists polled by Reuters expected a 0.4 percent increase. Excluding auto sales, retail sales were also down 0.1 percent versus forecasts for a 0.3 percent rise.
Earlier, the U.S. Labor Department said weekly jobless claims rose to 339,000 for the week ended June 7. Analysts had expected claims to drop to 326,000 after a surge to 337,000 the prior week.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was off its highs but up 25/32 at 98-1/32 to yield 6.78 percent. The bond had been up a full point shortly after the number.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 21/32 at 117-9/32. The September T-bond contract was up 20/32 at 111-7/32. The MOB spread was 194 ticks.
Thursday's active issues included Chicago, Ill., Board of Education 5-3/4 percent bonds of December 2027. The bonds were bid at a dollar price of 100-1/2 versus 100 at Wednesday's close.
Municipal supply remains scarce, another trader said.
"Municipals are very thin, I think people are looking to buy them pretty much across the board," he said.
Standard & Poor's Blue List, however, rose to $1.126 billion Thursday versus $992 million on Wednesday.
